meta.title: MedTech Meta Index
meta.description: A source-of-sources index for the authoritative public datasets, standards indexes, curated field atlas, and derived analytical datasets used by Baltimore MedTech.
meta.inclusion_rule: A component must have a named publisher or steward, a stable source or workbook route, a documented unit or analytical role, and explicit limitations. Restricted patient-level datasets are described only when a public component is actually registered.
meta.ranking_rule: Decision rank reflects proximity to measurable patient access and service delivery, not institutional prestige, scientific importance, dataset size, or moral value.

quality_tiers.B1: Curated scientific, semantic, or coding index based on named stewards
quality_tiers.B2: Curated extract from authoritative public statistics
quality_tiers.C1: Derived analytical dataset with inspectable inputs and method

limitations: The Meta Index is a catalog and evidence map, not a merged patient-provider fact table.
Source ranks reflect decision proximity; they are not universal quality scores.
Different sources use different populations, time periods, geographies, payer scopes, and units of observation.
A valid cross-source comparison still requires explicit joins, denominator alignment, deduplication, and missing-data analysis.

sources.unit_of_observation: Provider × HCPCS service × place of service
sources.decision_role: Measures services, beneficiaries, charges, allowed amounts, and payments realized in Original Medicare fee-for-service.
sources.quality_strength: Directly observes billed service output with standardized provider and HCPCS identifiers.
sources.principal_caveat: Excludes Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, commercial insurance, uninsured care, and suppressed small beneficiary cells.
sources.join_keys: NPI; HCPCS; provider geography; place of service

sources.evidence_type: Medicare enrollment and Care Compare publication
sources.decision_role: Locates enrolled clinicians, specialties, organizations, facilities, practice sites, and telehealth indicators.
sources.quality_strength: Current public provider roster with NPI, specialty, group, and location fields suitable for linkage.
sources.principal_caveat: Rows are not unique people, and enrollment does not establish appointment availability or acceptance of every payer.
sources.join_keys: NPI; organization PAC ID; enrollment ID; address
sources.dependencies: CMS enrollment and Care Compare systems

sources.unit_of_observation: Interactive provider, facility, location, specialty, and plan search result
sources.decision_role: Tests whether Medicaid-enrolled patients can identify providers and facilities associated with relevant HealthChoice access paths.
sources.quality_strength: Official Maryland Medicaid directory and program guidance focused on covered access.
sources.principal_caveat: The public interface is not a documented bulk API, and not every listed provider accepts every HealthChoice plan.
sources.join_keys: Provider identity; location; specialty; managed-care plan when exposed
sources.dependencies: Maryland Medicaid and HealthChoice directory operations

sources.decision_role: Verifies whether a provider was actively enrolled in Maryland Medicaid fee-for-service on a specified date.
sources.quality_strength: Official state verification source for provider enrollment status.
sources.principal_caveat: Active enrollment does not prove that a provider is accepting patients, accepting payment, or participating in every managed-care network.
sources.join_keys: Provider identifier; provider type; verification date

sources.decision_role: Measures Baltimore-area or Maryland employment, wages, and location quotients across medical occupations.
sources.quality_strength: Consistent occupational and geographic estimates suitable for labor-market comparison.
sources.principal_caveat: Generally excludes self-employed workers; broad occupations may not map cleanly to a specialty or clinical service line.
sources.join_keys: SOC occupation; metropolitan or state area; year
sources.dependencies: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics

sources.unit_of_observation: County or state × variable × reference year
sources.data_layer: Health resources, facilities, workforce, population, and context
sources.decision_role: Provides county-level context for workforce, facilities, population, utilization, expenditure, and socioeconomic comparisons.
sources.quality_strength: Broad, documented compilation designed for geographic health-resource analysis.
sources.principal_caveat: Reference years differ by variable, and the current workbook sheet exposes release metadata rather than unpacking every variable in-browser.
sources.join_keys: FIPS geography; variable identifier; reference year
sources.dependencies: HRSA AHRF and more than sixty contributing sources

sources.decision_role: Provides stable provider identifiers, taxonomy codes, names, and practice-location records for linkage and discovery.
sources.quality_strength: National identifier backbone with machine-readable taxonomy and address fields.
sources.principal_caveat: Enumeration is not evidence of licensure, credentialing, active clinical work, payer participation, or appointment supply.
sources.dependencies: National Plan and Provider Enumeration System

sources.authority_class: Baltimore MedTech extract from federal labor statistics
sources.decision_role: Prevents physician headcount from being presented as the complete service system by exposing selected therapy, imaging, radiation, and genetics occupations.
sources.quality_strength: Every row retains SOC code, official source, mapping strength, and field-specific scope warning.
sources.principal_caveat: Mapped national occupation totals are not dedicated specialty full-time equivalents and do not exhaust the care team.

sources.authority_class: Baltimore MedTech index of named standards stewards
sources.unit_of_observation: Terminology, exchange, imaging, genomics, or research-data system
sources.decision_role: Distinguishes clinical meaning, identifiers, exchange structures, imaging objects, genomic representation, and research models.
sources.quality_strength: Connects each system to its official steward, role, scope, identifiers, licensing context, and source links.
sources.principal_caveat: The index does not distribute licensed terminology content and mappings remain version-dependent.
sources.join_keys: System identifier; concept identifier; implementation profile
sources.dependencies: SNOMED CT; LOINC; RxNorm; FHIR; UMLS; DICOM; GA4GH VRS; OMOP CDM

sources.authority_class: Baltimore MedTech index of official code-system stewards
sources.data_layer: Diagnosis, procedure, product, claim context, and payment
sources.decision_role: Clarifies how ICD, CPT, HCPCS, NDC, revenue, place-of-service, local charge, and Maryland Medicaid layers relate without conflating them.
sources.quality_strength: Preserves steward, scope, identifier shape, licensing, role, and official source links.
sources.principal_caveat: Educational descriptions do not replace current licensed code sets, billing manuals, contracts, edits, or payer policy.
sources.join_keys: Code-system identifier; code; effective date; payer context
sources.dependencies: WHO; CDC; CMS; AMA; ADA; Maryland Medicaid; institutional charge systems

sources.authority_class: Baltimore MedTech crosswalk to named scientific and professional frameworks
sources.decision_role: Organizes medical science by anatomy, disease mechanism, method, biological scale, population, care setting, and translation rather than one rigid tree.
sources.quality_strength: Maintains parent-child relationships and crosswalk lenses to MeSH, ACGME, OECD FORD, NIH RCDC, and WHO-FIC.
sources.principal_caveat: It is a curated orientation atlas, not an official clinical terminology, certification list, or universal taxonomy.
sources.join_keys: Field ID; parent field; source-lens category
sources.dependencies: MeSH; ACGME; OECD FORD; NIH RCDC; WHO-FIC; Baltimore MedTech curation

sources.data_layer: Need, labor, funding, and application strategy
sources.decision_role: Places need, workforce, pipeline, funding, and digital-leverage signals in one inspectable field-level record.
sources.quality_strength: Retains definitions, years, sources, scope notes, and strategic interpretation for each metric.
sources.principal_caveat: The four example fields use unlike denominators and should not be treated as a universal league table.
sources.dependencies: Public need, workforce, pipeline, and NIH budget sources

sources.decision_role: Surfaces fields where selected need proxies appear to outrun selected physician workforce and entry-pipeline proxies.
sources.quality_strength: Formula, weights, raw ratios, normalized components, source data, and interpretive guardrails are exposed.
sources.principal_caveat: The score is relative within four unlike proxies and is not an absolute shortage threshold, access rate, or allocation rule.
sources.dependencies: Strategy field metrics; need-availability method; allied-care context
